## Item 2 — Records month stepper: disable future beyond the current month

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE 2026-07-08** (base behavior; = paywall doc §12 Phase 0 · Item 2). **Model: Sonnet, low effort.** Paywall gate for it — **paywall doc §8 / Q8.1** (free = last 12 months; premium extends the past) — still pending the entitlement infra.

**Change (base behavior, non-paywall):** the month steppers had **no cap in either direction**. The actual mechanism (the item's original line refs were stale): Records is the **transactions** feature — [TransactionsViewModel.nextMonth()](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsViewModel.kt#L94) steps `viewedMonth` via `MonthWindow.step`; the couple **Combined** view does the same ([CombinedViewModel.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/presentation/CombinedViewModel.kt#L166)). Both render the **shared** [core/ui/MonthStepperRow](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/MonthStepperRow.kt). Analysis is a *separate* stepper (`AnalysisPeriodRange`, multi-granularity).

**Built:** one tested predicate `MonthWindow.canStepForward(monthStart, today)` (strictly-before by `YearMonth`) is the single source of truth. `MonthStepperRow` gained a `canGoNext: Boolean = true` flag (disables the → button, mirroring Analysis's `PeriodStepper(canStep=…)`); Records + Combined each expose `canGoToNextMonth` on their UiState and **guard `nextMonth()`** as a backstop. JVM tests in `MonthWindowTest` (past→true, current/future→false, day-of-month ignored). No Room/schema/sync change.

**Open sub-questions — RESOLVED 2026-07-08 (scope decided with Alvin):**
- **Scope = Records + Combined** (both couple/personal month-ledgers with the identical empty-future wart + shared `MonthStepperRow`). **Analysis left uncapped** — ADR-0030 keeps it "steppable calendar buckets," and "current period" is ill-defined for QUARTER/ANNUAL/ALL_TIME.
- **Budgets + Recurring left uncapped** — future budgeting (duplicate-to-next-month, rollover) and recurring projections legitimately live in the future.

The premium "deeper past" extension (free −12mo → premium −12−n) is **gating** and waits on the entitlement infrastructure (paywall doc §6 sequencing).

## Item 3 — Analysis: Flow-generalization + Calendar month-stepper (grilled 2026-07-09)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `97cf5c7`** (both base behaviours; on-device verified by Alvin 2026-07-09). **Model: Sonnet, medium** for the two base-behaviour builds (they follow the existing Analysis pattern; window/bucket math is contained). Paywall gates (paywall doc §10.1), both now ✅ DONE: **`ANALYSIS_EXTENDED_RANGES` DONE `5ab69ea`** (paywall **Phase 2 · S10 sub-gate 2**, on-device verified — soft-gate on the existing 3M/6M/12M/ALL tabs via `AnalysisPeriod.isExtendedRange` + `PremiumGate.observeLocked`, locked tap → paywall, range unchanged); **`DEEP_HISTORY` DONE `4521293`** (paywall **Phase 2 · S10 sub-gate 3**, on-device verified — the −12mo back-wall on Records/Combined/Analysis-free-range steppers via `MonthWindow.canStepBack` / `AnalysisPeriodRange.canStepBack` on the shared anchor, back ← → 🔒 paywall affordance at the floor). Both 2026-07-11.
- **Built:** (A) `ExpenseFlowCalculator` generalized to any range — daily buckets for 1D/1W/1M/3M, monthly for 6M/12M/ALL (`FlowBucketMode`); ALL anchors to `currentUser.createdAt`'s month (not the 2000 sentinel); budget line + budget-remaining dropped; `FlowMetricsCalculator` → avg/day vs avg/month + projected (current, bounded, multi-bucket only); chart draws pre-computed axis ticks (`FlowAxisLabel`); 1D → "range too short to chart" state. (B) `AnalysisScreen` shows all three sub-tabs under every range with the Calendar⟺1M coupling (tap/swipe onto Calendar snaps range→1M via `LaunchedEffect`; non-1M range while on Calendar bounces to Donut); `AnalysisPeriodRange.canStepForward` forward-caps 1D/1W/1M (3M/6M/12M uncapped, ALL non-steppable), `next()` guarded as backstop.
- **Scope add beyond the original grill:** a **"vs previous period"** look-back metric (`FlowComparisonCalculator` — signed %/direction vs the prior same-length window, "New" when no baseline, skipped for ALL) now sits beside Avg so past periods aren't single-stat (`projected` is null on a completed period). Alvin's call 2026-07-09 after seeing the lonely Avg row — this is the grill's sanctioned free look-back (pure live re-read, no storage).
- **Files touched:** `domain/model/ExpenseFlowData.kt` (+`FlowBucketMode`), `domain/usecase/{ExpenseFlowCalculator,FlowMetricsCalculator,AnalysisPeriodRange}.kt`, new `domain/usecase/FlowComparisonCalculator.kt`, `presentation/{AnalysisUiState,AnalysisViewModel,AnalysisScreen}.kt`, `presentation/components/ExpenseFlowChart.kt`. `ObserveBudgetsUseCase` dropped from the ViewModel (Flow no longer reads budgets). No Room/schema/sync change (Room stays v23).
- **Tests added:** rewrote `ExpenseFlowCalculatorTest` (daily/monthly buckets, ALL-from-registration, current-bucket marker) + `FlowMetricsCalculatorTest` (elapsed-vs-full avg, projection suppression, perMonth), new `FlowComparisonCalculatorTest`, `canStepForward` cases in `AnalysisPeriodRangeTest`.

**History — the "rolling ranges" approach was tried and reverted (2026-07-08 → 2026-07-09).** The first plan was to *build* net-new trailing "Last 3M / Last 6M / All time" windows and gate those. It built green but Alvin rejected it on sight: a separate trailing-window row stacked confusingly beside the existing calendar **3M / 6M / 12M / ALL** tabs (which are quarter/half/year). Fully reverted (working tree back to `bfd908a`).

**The gate (decided 2026-07-08/09), replacing the build.** The premium lever is a **soft gate on the *existing* calendar tabs** — free = **1D / 1W / 1M**, premium = **3M / 6M / 12M / ALL** (tap a locked tab → paywall). No new range built → wire-only paywall work (Phase 2 S10), waits on the entitlement infra. Not a base-behaviour build.

**The base-behaviour work that DOES remain (grilled 2026-07-09, unrelated to the gate).** Two changes to the Analysis sub-tabs (Donut / Flow / Calendar), which today only render under 1M ([AnalysisScreen.kt:130](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/analysis/presentation/AnalysisScreen.kt#L130) `MonthTabLayout`); Donut already renders for every range.

**(A) Flow → all ranges.** Flow is MONTH-only today (`ExpenseFlowCalculator` / `FlowMetricsCalculator` hardwire one month via `lengthOfMonth()` + `dayOfMonth-1`). Generalize it:
- Shape everywhere = **cumulative spend curve + avg + projected**. **Budget line + budget-remaining dropped** — the one monthly-only wart; budget-vs-spend is the Budgets tab's job. 🅿️ *Parked: Alvin may reintroduce a budget overlay later, once a clean way is found.*
- **Buckets:** daily for 1D/1W/1M/3M; monthly for 6M/12M/ALL. Cumulative running total either way.
- **avg:** `avg/day` on the daily ranges, `avg/month` on the monthly ranges. **ALL's denominator = the user's registration date** (`currentUser.createdAt`, already in the ViewModel), *not* the fixed `ALL_TIME_START = 2000-01-01` sentinel — else avg ÷ ~9,700 days ≈ 0.
- **projected = pace × full-period length**; shown for the **current in-progress period only** (on a past period `pace×length` = the actual total, redundant with the Summary card); **disabled for ALL** (unbounded, no length). 🅿️ *Parked: if ever pinned on past periods, label it "Total," not "Projected."*
- **Look-back comparison** (this quarter vs last, etc.) is free and needs **no storage** — Analysis is a pure live read, so any past period recomputes from the ledger; `avg/day` (shown on every period) + the Summary-card totals carry the comparison.
- **1D:** cumulative curve is a single point → show avg/day + a short "range too short to chart" state, not a lonely dot.

**(B) Calendar → 1M-coupled month behaviour.** The Calendar day-grid is inherently monthly. Grilled rules:
- All three sub-tabs always visible under every top range. **Calendar ⟺ 1M coupling:** tapping **Calendar** from any non-1M range auto-snaps the range to **1M**; tapping any non-1M range tab while on Calendar bounces back to **Donut** (tapping 1M while on Calendar is a no-op). So Calendar only ever runs under 1M → it **shares the 1M month stepper**, no separate stepper.
- **Stepper gating on the shared *anchor*, across all free ranges (1D/1W/1M):** forward cap = current period (reuse `MonthWindow.canStepForward` from Item 2); back floor = **−12 months free, −13+ premium** (`DEEP_HISTORY`). Enforced on the anchor so 1W/1D can't back-door the −12 wall. Premium = unlimited history. **This refines Item 2**, which left Analysis steppers uncapped — 1D/1W/1M now get the forward cap (their "current period" is well-defined); the premium longer tabs (3M/6M/12M/ALL) stay forward-uncapped.

**Verify:** JVM unit tests for the generalized Flow window/bucket/avg/projected math (mirror `AnalysisPeriodRangeTest`) + the shared-anchor cap predicate. On-device: Flow renders sensibly on each range (1D short-state; monthly buckets on 6M+); Calendar↔1M auto-snap + bounce behave; free stepping is bounded `[−12mo … today]` in every free granularity.

**Sequence:** the two base behaviours (A, B) build now — dormant-safe, no entitlement dependency. The soft-gate on 3M/6M/12M/ALL + the −12/−13 `DEEP_HISTORY` wall are wired later with the paywall infra (Phase 2 S10).

**DEEP_HISTORY scope — Budgets & Recurring stay uncapped (decided 2026-07-11).** When S10 landed, Alvin flagged that the **Budgets** month stepper has no cap at all. Confirmed intentional, no change: its **forward** arrow must stay open (setting next month's budget — duplicate-to-next-month / rollover, per Item 2), and its **backward** side is deliberately *not* walled — Budgets is a planning surface, not a history-browser, so the −12mo `DEEP_HISTORY` gate (grilled to Records + Combined + Analysis free ranges only) does not extend to it. **Recurring** likewise stays uncapped (its calendar *view* is already premium via S9 `RECURRING_CALENDAR`; rules aren't history browsing). Do not add a stepper cap to Budgets/Recurring.

## Item 4 — Notes: enforce a character limit

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `6e95238`** (2026-07-11, on-device verified by Alvin; = paywall doc §12 **Phase 0 · Item 4**, which it **closes**). **Model: Sonnet** (built on Opus, but pure pattern-following — no open design calls). The base **existence** of a limit shipped here; the **5,000 vs 50,000 tier split** — paywall **Phase 2 · S10 sub-gate 1** — is now also **✅ DONE `f0da7e4`** (2026-07-11; see the "S10 split" section at the end of this item).

**Change:** notes previously had **no character limit** ([NotesViewModel.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/notes/presentation/NotesViewModel.kt) only truncates the list *preview*, not the note body). Added a real limit in the note editor: counts the reader-visible (WYSIWYG) body length, surfaces an `n/limit` counter near the cap (reddens when over — mirrors the attachment `n/3` counter from [V1.6.4](v1.6.4.md) Item 3), and **hard-blocks growth** by trimming any overflow at the cursor back to the cap (trims a paste to fit, rejects the extra keystroke; body only, skipped for read-only partner notes). Alvin's caveat stays on the record: 5,000 free is tight for rich text — adjust if it bites; a separate observation from the on-device pass — the rich editor lags only past ~400k chars, so even the 50k premium ceiling is comfortably responsive.

- **Design — ships dormant (S8/S9 pattern):** the base ceiling is `NoteCharLimit.DEFAULT_MAX = 50_000` (= the *premium* max), so in normal use the counter/trim are invisible; nothing changes for anyone until S10 lowers the free tier to 5,000. The `OutlinedRichTextEditor` exposes no `maxLength`/`onValueChange` hook (verified against the decompiled lib — it is fully state-driven), so enforcement rides the `RichTextState` API reactively: `annotatedString.text.length` for the live count + `removeTextRange` to strip overflow at the cursor. S10 feeds the resolved per-tier limit into this mechanism; counting + trim are unchanged (with one freeze-safety addition, below).
- **Files touched:** `NoteCharLimit.kt` (new, pure boundary math), `NoteEditorScreen.kt` (live count + counter UI + reactive trim block), `NoteCharLimitTest.kt` (new).
- **Tests added:** 5 tier-1 JVM cases (`NoteCharLimitTest` — overflow/isOver/shouldShowCounter boundaries + the dormant-at-50k assertion); editor wiring is UI, verified by running. No Room/schema change (stays **v25**).

**S10 split (Phase 2 · S10 sub-gate 1) — ✅ DONE `f0da7e4` (2026-07-11). Model: Opus (a real freeze-safety design call, not pure wire-only).** The editor's body ceiling now tracks the entitlement-resolved tier limit instead of the hardcoded `DEFAULT_MAX`.
- **The seam:** new `PremiumGate.observeLimit(scope, limitOf): Flow<Int>` — sibling to S9's `observeLocked` and S7's `checkCap`, but it resolves a **concrete ceiling both tiers honour** (`PlanLimits.resolve(hasAccess = !shouldLock, overrides)` → PREMIUM unless locked, else FREE), not a boolean or a create-time decision. `NoteEditorViewModel` collects `observeLimit(Scope.INDIVIDUAL, PlanLimits::maxNoteChars)` into `NoteEditorUiState.noteCharLimit` (default `DEFAULT_MAX`, so pre-emission / **dormant** = premium 50k = byte-identical to before).
- **Freeze-safety (the design call, kept):** a literal constant-swap would have **truncated an existing >5k note down to 5k on open** the moment the free cap drops below its length — the trim `snapshotFlow` fires on seed, sees `length > limit`, and strips the overflow. That is **silent user-data deletion on flip day** (a 40k note authored while premium → chopped to 5k), i.e. exactly the T1-freeze / paywall §10.7 worst-case ("a finance app that hides a user's data on flip day"). Fix: a new pure `NoteCharLimit.effectiveLimit(tierLimit, existingLength) = max(…)` — the editor captures the **seeded body length** once and enforces `max(tierLimit, seededLength)`, so an over-cap note is **frozen at its current length** (read-only-for-growth), never truncated; only *new* growth past the frozen ceiling is blocked. A within-cap note just gets the plain tier limit. The trim `LaunchedEffect` is re-keyed on the resolved ceiling so a live enforcement flip re-evaluates.
- **Files touched (split):** `core/entitlement/PremiumGate.kt` (+`observeLimit`), `NoteCharLimit.kt` (+`effectiveLimit`), `NoteEditorUiState.kt` (+`noteCharLimit`), `NoteEditorViewModel.kt` (inject `PremiumGate` + collect), `NoteEditorScreen.kt` (seeded-length capture + `effectiveLimit` ceiling + re-keyed trim).
- **Tests (split):** +6 tier-1 JVM cases — 4 `observeLimit` (`PremiumGateTest`: dormant→50k, enforced-free→5k, enforced-premium→50k, individual-ignores-partner) + 2 `effectiveLimit` (`NoteCharLimitTest`: within-cap = tier, over-cap frozen = no truncation but still can't grow). `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green. No Room/schema change (stays **v25**). **On-device (enforcement ON, staging):** a fresh note caps at 5k with the counter; an existing >5k note opens intact and only can't grow. Dormant behaviour unchanged.

## Item 6 — Delete account (Play policy requirement) 🔴

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `9e0614e`** (2026-07-13, on-device verified by Alvin). **Model: Opus** (Alvin's session pick; from-spec Sonnet-class work — every design call was locked in the grill). Full design in **[ADR-0045](../adr/0045-delete-account-hard-delete-rpc.md)** (grilled on Opus; every open question below resolved, several against live-staging verification). Non-paywall (compliance, not a tier lever). No Room/schema-version change (stays **v25**).
- **As built:** exactly the grilled shape, with one simplification (storage, below). **Server:** `delete_account()` SECURITY DEFINER RPC (migration `2026-07-12_delete_account.sql` = infra #19 — applied + verified live on staging: `security_definer`, owner `postgres`, `authenticated`-only execute, `anon` denied). Body = `perform unpair()` when paired → delete the caller's `storage.objects` rows → `delete from auth.users where id = auth.uid()`, one atomic transaction; the FK cascade physically removes the rest. **Client (`feature/settings`):** `DeleteUserAccountUseCase` (password re-auth gate) → `AccountDeletionRepository`/`Impl` (RPC = point of no return → best-effort `clearLocalSession` → `NonCancellable` wipe-with-retry) → `SupabaseAccountDeletionRemoteSource`; new `AuthRepository.clearLocalSession()` (throw-free local teardown via `client.auth.clearSession()`, verified in supabase-kt 3.6.0); ProfileScreen destructive "Delete account" row + Item 16-pattern dialog (online-gated, unpair notice when paired); WorkManager-cancel before the RPC. **Storage simplified to RPC-only** (Alvin's "don't make it complicated"): the RPC makes every receipt/note file permanently inaccessible by deleting its `storage.objects` row; the grilled client-side Storage-API pre-delete was **dropped** — its only gain was GC'ing orphaned-but-unreachable physical blobs (add it back if physical-blob GC is ever wanted). **Files touched:** `feature/auth` {`AuthRepository`, `AuthRepositoryImpl`}, `feature/settings` {`domain/repository/AccountDeletionRepository`, `domain/usecase/DeleteUserAccountUseCase`, `data/AccountDeletionRepositoryImpl`, `data/remote/{AccountDeletionRemoteSource, SupabaseAccountDeletionRemoteSource}`, `di/SettingsModule`, `presentation/{ProfileUiState, ProfileViewModel, ProfileScreen}`}, `supabase/{migrations/2026-07-12_delete_account.sql, schema.sql}`, `CONTEXT.md` (+"Delete account" term), `docs/adr/0045`. **Tests:** +6 tier-1 JVM — `DeleteUserAccountUseCaseTest` (×2, re-auth gate: correct → deletes, wrong → throws + never deletes) + `AccountDeletionRepositoryImplTest` (×4 teardown ordering: RPC-first, RPC-throws-aborts-with-no-wipe, clearSession-throws-still-wipes, wipe-retry) + the existing `FakeAuthRepository` given the new interface method; `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green. **Still pending (Alvin, manual — the web half of the Play requirement, below):** `delete-account.html` + Play Console Data safety form URL.
- **Why it's near-mandatory:** Google Play's User Data policy requires an **in-app account-deletion path** (plus a **web link** to request deletion without reinstalling). Right now Profile → Account ([ProfileScreen.kt:107-115](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/settings/presentation/ProfileScreen.kt#L107-L115)) shows the email **read-only** — there is no delete. The existing `DeleteAccountUseCase` is for *financial* accounts — the new use case is named **`DeleteUserAccountUseCase`** to dodge the collision.

**Design (grilled 2026-07-12 — ADR-0045 is authoritative, summary here):**
- **Hard delete, the one sanctioned ADR-0010 exception.** Tombstones exist for other sync consumers; unpair-first removes the only one (the partner) through the normal dissolution, so nothing is left for a tombstone to inform. Soft-delete would fail "delete my data" and squat on the email.
- **One `delete_account()` SECURITY DEFINER RPC, not an edge function** (verified: `postgres` — owner of `unpair()` et al. — has DELETE on `auth.users`; no service role needed). Body: `perform unpair()` when paired (reuse, never inline) → `storage.objects` backstop delete (`receipts` + `note-images`, `{uid}/%` prefix) → `delete from auth.users where id = auth.uid()`. **One atomic transaction**; the verified FK cascade (every owned table + GoTrue's own session tables) physically removes everything else.
- **Partner aftermath = exactly normal unpair** (verified in code): `WatchUnpairUseCase` keys off the partner's own users row `couple_id` set→null + the bell — never the couples tombstone — so the creator-deletion cascade hard-deleting that tombstone pre-pull is harmless.
- **Storage** (`storage.objects` has **no** FK to `auth.users` — the cascade misses files): client best-effort Storage-API batch delete first (paths enumerated from Room `note_images.storage_path` + `transaction_images`; existing `FOR ALL` owner RLS suffices, verified), RPC SQL delete as the in-transaction backstop making anything missed permanently unreachable.
- **Client gate:** Item 16's exact pattern — **online-only** (`ConnectivityObserver` live-disables the confirm while offline; no offline attempt ever) + **password re-auth** (`AuthRepository.signIn`) inline in **one** confirm dialog (plain-words warning incl. the unpair effect when paired). No typed-DELETE ceremony, **no grace period** — immediate.
- **Orchestration (RPC = point of no return):** cancel WorkManager sync → re-auth → storage best-effort → `rpc("delete_account")` → best-effort `signOut()` (falls back to local session clear — the server session is already cascade-dead) → `LocalDataWiper.wipe()` under the existing `NonCancellable`+retry wrapper → auth graph. **Deliberately no `pushOnly()` first** (unpushed edits are about to be deleted by definition; a wedged push must never block deletion — Item 20's lesson).
- **Side effects accepted:** `analytics_events` history cascades away (correct for compliance; no "account_deleted" client event — it would delete itself). Re-registration with the same email works by construction (the `auth.users` row is what holds email uniqueness).

**Manual sub-tasks (Alvin, booked with this item — the web half of the Play requirement):**
- Author a static **`delete-account.html`** on the legal GitHub Pages site (what's deleted, the in-app path, `mailto:` request contact with a stated ~30-day window; fulfilled manually via the Supabase dashboard — the cascade makes that one delete).
- Enter that URL in the Play Console **Data safety form**.

**Build checklist:** migration `2026-07-12_delete_account.sql` + `schema.sql` end-state (grants per `unpair()` precedent) · `feature/settings`: `DeleteUserAccountUseCase` + small remote/storage ports (mirror Item 16's shape) · ProfileScreen destructive "Delete account" row + Item 16-pattern dialog · amend `CONTEXT.md` ("Delete account" term, distinct from "Reset finances") · JVM tests on the orchestration order (re-auth failure aborts pre-RPC; storage failure doesn't abort; RPC failure aborts with no wipe; post-RPC teardown proceeds even when `signOut()` throws). **Verify on staging:** solo delete, paired-creator delete + partner lands in normal-unpair state, paired-non-creator delete, re-register the freed email; confirm storage objects gone and the confirm is disabled offline.

## Item 9 — Sync & Data status 🟡

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `4fc5696`** (2026-07-14, on-device verified by Alvin). **Model: Sonnet, low–medium** (grill downgraded the booked "Sonnet→Opus" — the sync-layer touch is additive: one optional injected store + one write line, no orchestration change; built on Opus this session). Non-paywall. No ADR needed (follows the `ClockOffsetStore` precedent). No Room/schema change (stays **v25**).
- **Why:** we are **offline-first with cloud sync**, yet Settings surfaces nothing about sync — no "Sync now", no "Last synced …", no error state. Grill finding: `SyncEngine.state` (`Idle/Syncing/Success(at)/Error(message)`) **already exists and is write-only** — no UI renders it (the ARCHITECTURE §6 "shown subtly" was never wired).

**Grilled design (2026-07-13):**
- **Surface: a "Sync" card in PersonalizeScreen** (no sub-screen — three lines don't earn a nav route): **Sync now** button + **"Last synced X ago"** + a status line (*Syncing… / Offline / Couldn't sync*). **No pending-changes count** — deliberately excluded: a naive 15-table `pendingSync=1` count would read "1 waiting" *forever* on Item 20's benign un-pushable orphans; an honest count needs the `isLocallyPushable`/`isCoupleRowPushable` predicate filtering (Kotlin, not SQL). Book it later as its own item only if testers ask.
- **Persistence:** new `core/sync/data/SyncStatusStore` (DataStore-backed `lastSyncedAt`), **optionally injected into `SyncEngine`** (nullable param, `ClockOffsetStore` sibling — existing tests untouched), written at the exact line `state` flips to `Success`. Survives restarts (the in-memory flow boots `Idle`, so without this the card reads "—" on every cold open). Background WorkManager syncs write it for free (same `sync()`).
- **Semantics:** "last synced" = last successful **full `sync()`** — the micro-paths (`pushOnly`/`pullOnly`) stay state-silent by design (they already are). "Sync now" = `syncEngine.sync()`, identical to pull-to-refresh; single-flight coalescing already handles double-taps; button disables into "Syncing…" while `state == Syncing`.
- **Errors: friendly copy only** ("Couldn't sync — try again"), per Alvin — **no raw-message caption**; instead the engine's error path logs the raw exception at **`Log.w`** (not `Log.d` — suppressed on the test device) so a tester report is pinpointable via logcat/staging without UI noise. `Error` is transient — not persisted, a reopen shows just "Last synced X ago".
- **Offline flavor (reuses Item 16 infra):** via `ConnectivityObserver`, the status line reads "Offline — changes sync when you reconnect" and **Sync now disables** (same disable-with-hint pattern as Items 16/6).
- **Files:** `SyncEngine.kt` (+optional `SyncStatusStore` + one write + `Log.w`), new `core/sync/data/SyncStatusStore.kt`, sync DI module, `PersonalizeScreen/ViewModel/UiState` (card + observe `state`/store/connectivity), small relative-time helper.
- **Tier-1 tests (sync layer → mandatory):** store written on `Success`, untouched on failure; store round-trip; coalesced runs don't double-write.

**Verify:** on-device — Sync now spins then "Last synced just now"; kill + reopen → timestamp survives; airplane mode → "Offline" + disabled button; force an error (bad session) → friendly copy + raw exception in logcat.

**As-built (`4fc5696`, 2026-07-14):** matches the grilled design. New `core/sync/data/SyncStatusStore` (DataStore-backed `lastSyncedAt` in the existing `sync_prefs`, `open` so a test can count writes), optionally injected into `SyncEngine` (nullable param, `ClockOffsetStore` sibling — existing engine tests untouched) and written **inside a `runCatching`** at the exact line `state` flips to `Success` (a DataStore hiccup must not fail a sync that actually succeeded); `pushOnly`/`pullOnly` never write it. The engine's `catch` now logs the raw cause at `Log.w` (device-visible) + adds a private `TAG`. `PersonalizeViewModel` observes `SyncEngine.state` + `SyncStatusStore.observe()` + `ConnectivityObserver.observe()` in a **second** `combine` (the existing snapshot combine is at its 5-flow max) into four new `PersonalizeUiState` fields; `syncNow()` = `syncEngine.sync()`. The "Sync" card sits under Finance in `PersonalizeScreen`; one priority-ordered status line (Syncing… → Offline hint → "Couldn't sync — try again"), Sync-now disabled offline/while-syncing. New pure `core/ui/RelativeTime.kt` (`relativeTimeLabel`, coarse minute/hour/day). **One call beyond the grill:** `LocalDataWiper` now also clears the timestamp on sign-out (ADR-0021) — otherwise the next account's Settings would read the previous user's "Last synced X ago". +5 `SyncEngineTest` (persist-on-Success, skip-on-failure, round-trip+clear, coalesced-writes-once, micro-paths-never-write), +3 `RelativeTimeTest`, `LocalDataWiperTest` extended; 883 unit tests green. On-device verified by Alvin.

## Item 10 — Finance preferences 🟡

- **Status:** PLANNED. Split by weight. Non-paywall (base behavior).
- **(a) Default account for new transactions — Model: Sonnet.** DataStore pref, consumed by the Add Transaction editor to pre-select the account. Light, self-contained.
- **(b) Budget cycle start day (monthly reset ≠ calendar 1st) — ✅ DONE `618cc25`** (2026-07-14). **Model: Sonnet, medium** (as scoped; built on Opus). Design locked in **[ADR-0046](../adr/0046-budget-cycle-start-day.md)**. Still its own slice — was not folded into (a).

**10b grilled design (ADR-0046 is authoritative, summary):** a "Budget month starts on day N" setting (default 1 = byte-identical to today) for **payday-aligned budget months** (PH kinsenas/katapusan — the 15th/30th). **Scope: budgets only** — Records/Combined/Analysis and the paywall stepper predicates (`MonthWindow`, `AnalysisPeriodRange`) stay calendar-month, untouched; recurring is unaffected by construction (rules step from their own `nextDate`, never a month boundary — the original booking's "recurring date math" worry was wrong). **Personal budgets only** — the shared couple budget stays calendar (a per-user cycle can't bind a two-user row; `CombinedViewModel` computes shared spent off the calendar `monthKey` and never calls `BudgetProgressCalculator.spent`, so it's calendar by construction — pin with a test). **Local DataStore** (`finance_prefs`, privacy-mode pattern) — partner never sees personal budgets, so no synced column; reinstall loses the pref → calendar months until re-set, self-healing. **Mechanism: keep `Budget.yearMonth` as an opaque cycle key, reinterpret only its window** — label = the cycle *starting* that month (`"2026-07"` @ day 15 = Jul 15 → Aug 14), boundaries computed statelessly per label (`K.atDay(min(startDay, K.lengthOfMonth()))`, never iterated `plusMonths` — the drift trap), so rollover/cap/duplicate/alerts keep working on consecutive labels untouched, zero schema/Room/sync change (stays **v25**). **Days 1–31 with short-month clamping** (30 must stay allowed — katapusan; clamped boundaries stay contiguous; 31 ≡ last-day-of-month). **Setting changes are retroactive + stateless** (reinterpret all history; derived spent/rollover make it write-nothing and fully reversible; caption: "Applies to all budget months, including past ones"; one-time duplicate budget-alert re-fire on change day accepted). **UI:** PersonalizeScreen row under a new "Finance" section (10a lands beside it later) → 1–31 picker dialog; Budgets header shows the cycle's date range ("Jul 15 – Aug 14") when day ≠ 1. **Cycle-aware call sites (full set, verified):** `BudgetProgressCalculator`/`yearMonthKey`, `BudgetsViewModel`, `CheckBudgetAlertsUseCase` + `BudgetAlertWorker`, `ResetBudgetRolloverUseCase`. **Tier-1 tests:** day-1 ≡ `yearMonthKey`; day-15 boundary bucketing; day-31/30 Feb clamp contiguity (no gap/overlap); spent + rollover chain under non-1 day; alert current-cycle; shared-budget-stays-calendar pin.

**As-built (`618cc25`, 2026-07-14):** matches the grilled design above with one UI narrowing decided post-grill — the day picker offers **5 presets** (1st/10th/15th/25th/End of month) rather than a free 1–31 grid, since those are the only paydays that matter in practice; the mechanism underneath still accepts any 1–31 (End of month stores 31, which the existing clamp already reduces to each month's last day, so no extra code was needed for it). New `BudgetCycle` object (`cycleKey`/`window`, pure); `startDay` threaded through `BudgetProgressCalculator.spent`/`effectiveLimit`, `CheckBudgetAlertsUseCase`; `BudgetAlertWorker` split into two `checkBudgetAlerts` calls (personal on the cycle, shared couple budget forced to `startDay = 1`) since a per-user cycle can't bind a two-user row; `BudgetsViewModel` re-anchors the stepper to the current cycle on open and renders the header as a date range ("Jul 15 – Aug 14") when day ≠ 1; new `finance_prefs` DataStore + `BudgetStartDayRepository`/use cases (privacy-mode pattern); Settings gains a "Finance" section with the preset dialog. No schema/Room change (stays **v25**). +11 tier-1 JVM tests (`BudgetCycleTest` incl. a full-year day-30 contiguity sweep; `BudgetCycleSpentTest` incl. the shared-stays-calendar pin); `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green. **On-device verified** (emulator, Medium_Phone AVD, testdev15@iponlove.com — a real paired-couple staging account): preset dialog + instant persistence, header re-anchor to "Jun 15 – Jul 14", rollover chain carrying correctly across the cycle boundary on real multi-category transaction data, the shared couple budget staying on plain calendar "July 2026" simultaneously with the personal cycle view, and full reversibility back to "1st (calendar month)" with the same transactions re-bucketing accordingly. The End-of-month short-month clamp was not separately re-driven on-device (already covered by the JVM contiguity sweep).

## Item 13 — Nickname: rename "Name" → "Nickname" + hard-cap (10 chars, letters + spaces) 🟢

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `4681267`** (2026-07-11, on-device verified by Alvin). **Model: Sonnet, low effort.** Non-paywall. Requested by Alvin 2026-07-07.
- **Independent** — pure label + validation change, no schema/sync/data change (`display_name` identifier is unchanged; only user-facing labels + the length/charset rule change).
- **As built:** matches the plan below as written — `AuthCredentials.MAX_NAME_LENGTH` 50→10 + the letters+spaces charset check on `validateName`, plus a new shared `filterNameInput()` live-filter (truncate-as-you-type, not just submit-time rejection) reused by both `ProfileViewModel.onNameChange` and `AuthViewModel.onNameChange`. All label copy updated. `core/ui/TextEllipsis.kt` (`String.ellipsize(max)`) applied at all three `PartnerDebtScreen.kt` partner-name sites (NetSummaryCard, DebtCard header, the "Add a debt" direction chips — the acute case, which also got the `maxLines=1`/`Ellipsis` backstop), capped at 15 display chars. +9 tier-1 JVM tests (`AuthCredentialsTest` + new `TextEllipsisTest`); `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green.

**Request:** shorten and re-label the user's name so combined-view attribution stays tidy: rename every user-facing **"Name"** label to **"Nickname"**, and hard-cap the value at **10 characters, letters + spaces only** (no digits/symbols; a space counts toward the 10 — decided 2026-07-07).

**Change:**
- **Validation (single chokepoint):** [AuthCredentials.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/auth/domain/usecase/AuthCredentials.kt) `validateName` is shared by both `SignUpUseCase` and `UpdateDisplayNameUseCase`. Set `MAX_NAME_LENGTH = 10` and add a letters+spaces rule (`^[\p{L} ]+$` — keeps accented letters; reject anything else, still reject blank), still throwing `AuthException(AuthError.INVALID_NAME)`.
- **Live input filter** (truncate to 10 + strip disallowed chars in `onValueChange`) at the two entry fields: [ProfileScreen.kt:71](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/settings/presentation/ProfileScreen.kt#L71) (via `ProfileViewModel.onNameChange`) and [AuthScreen.kt:97](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/auth/presentation/AuthScreen.kt#L97) (via `AuthViewModel.onNameChange`).
- **Label copy → "Nickname":** ProfileScreen section header `"Display name"`→`"Nickname"` (:61), field label `"Name"`→`"Nickname"` (:71), button `"Save name"`→`"Save nickname"` (:85); AuthScreen field `"Your name"`→`"Your nickname"` (:97) and error `"Enter your name (up to 50 characters)"`→`"Enter a nickname (letters only, up to 10 characters)"` (:212). Read-only display surfaces (combined view, couple overview, add-txn partner label, savings/debt/notes partner labels) reference `displayName` internally — **no change**.
- Dev-phase, staging-only: **no backfill** for existing over-long test names (they just can't re-save until shortened — acceptable).

**Long-name resilience (added 2026-07-07, from Alvin's tester note — the app must survive names longer than 10):** the cap only governs *this* user's own nickname. A **partner's** name is synced from *their* device via the redacting view (and pre-limit test data exists), so a long partner name still reaches the UI and must not break layout — the cap is not a substitute for defensive display.
- **Acute case (reported):** the Partner Debt **"Add a debt"** dialog — the two direction `IponFilterChip`s `"I owe $partnerName"` / `"$partnerName owes me"` ([PartnerDebtScreen.kt:279-290](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/partnerdebt/presentation/PartnerDebtScreen.kt#L279-L290)) sit side-by-side in a plain `Row` with no wrap/width constraint, so a long `$partnerName` overflows the dialog (matches the screenshot: `"xxxxxxlong name herexxxxxxxxx owes me"` runs off the edge).
- **Fix:** add a small reusable `String.ellipsize(max)` display helper in `core/ui/` (generic per the scalability principle) and truncate the interpolated *name* (not the whole label — keep "owes me"/"I owe" readable) at the chip labels + the summary/debt-card headers ([:144](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/partnerdebt/presentation/PartnerDebtScreen.kt#L144), [:153](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/partnerdebt/presentation/PartnerDebtScreen.kt#L153), [:181](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/partnerdebt/presentation/PartnerDebtScreen.kt#L181)); add `maxLines = 1, overflow = Ellipsis` as a backstop.
- **Audit** the other partner-name interpolation sites (combined view, couple overview, add-txn "Paid for {name}", savings-goal detail, notes) — most are single `Text` lines inside `fillMaxWidth` Columns that wrap safely rather than break alignment, so the debt chips are the priority; apply the same helper anywhere a long name is squeezed into a horizontal Row.

**Verify:** `AuthCredentials` unit tests (10-char boundary, letters+spaces pass, digit/symbol/blank reject, trim); `String.ellipsize` unit test. On-device: sign-up + Profile edit both enforce the cap and every label reads "Nickname"; **and** with a long *partner* name (>10, e.g. an un-updated test account), the Partner Debt "Add a debt" dialog chips stay aligned and don't clip.

## Item 16 — "Restart fresh": reset finances from Settings

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `e1c01b2`** (2026-07-12, on-device verified by Alvin). **Model: Sonnet.** Non-paywall. Bumped down from Post-V1 Horizon #13, 2026-07-07. **Re-grilled 2026-07-12** after Alvin's first on-device test — the grill **reversed the scope** (see below), and the code was reworked to match. No Room/schema change (stays **v25**).

**Request:** a user-facing way to reset their own financial data and start over, without deleting the account itself (distinct from Item 6 "Delete account" — they share only the generic `bulkRestamp` helper).

**Design — reworked on the 2026-07-12 grill (supersedes the original ADR-0037 / [v1.6.2.md](v1.6.2.md) Item 1 shape).** The mental model shifted from *"wipe the money-movement rows, keep structure, land on opening balance"* to **"keep the whole configuration, zero every peso."** Reset now does exactly two owned-row mutations, atomic in one `LocalTransactionRunner.run`, then one push:
1. **Soft-delete the user's transactions** (tombstone + push) — clears history.
2. **Zero `opening_balance` on the user's personal accounts** (an *update*; archived included, shared couple accounts skipped since they carry a null `user_id`) — so balances read ₱0 once the ledger is empty.

**Kept untouched (the reversals from the original):** **budgets** (limits stay; "spent" → ₱0 for free, being derived from wiped transactions), **recurring rules** (forward-looking config; deterministic-UUID materialization means a wiped occurrence can't resurrect, and the catch-up already advances `next_date` past today, so no backfill), **savings goals + all contributions/progress** (accumulated value, not clutter; never fed balances; and wiping them was the *only* part that reached shared couple data — so keeping them makes reset touch **zero** partner data), plus categories, notes, and all couple/shared state. **`opening_balance` → ₱0** is itself a reversal of the original ADR-0037 dec. 3 (which preserved it).

**Grill decisions (2026-07-12):** (1) zero balances, don't preserve opening balance; (2) retain budgets; (3) retain recurring rules untouched — no `next_date` manipulation needed; (4) **keep all savings progress** (Option 3 — drop `goal_contributions` from the wipe entirely); (5) accept the rollover-recompute consequence as-is; (6) keep password re-auth **and add an explicit online-only block** — a new reusable `core/network/ConnectivityObserver` disables the confirm with "You need an internet connection to reset" while offline (Level 1), rather than the implicit re-auth `NETWORK` error; (7) a per-goal "Reset progress" convenience action was considered and **left to the existing delete-goal / delete-contribution controls** (not booked).

**As built:** new `core/network/ConnectivityObserver` (reactive `observe()` + one-shot `isOnline()`, `NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET`); generic `core/sync/bulkRestamp` (fetch owned → per-row monotonic stamp → upsert; replaced the earlier `bulkSoftDelete`, reusable by a future delete-account); `core/sync/LocalTransactionRunner` (testable seam over `IponDatabase.withTransaction`); `ResetFinancesRepository`/`Impl` (2 mutations via `bulkRestamp`, atomic + push); `PreviewResetFinancesUseCase` + `ResetFinancesUseCase` (password re-auth via `AuthRepository.signIn` before touching anything); `AccountDao.activeOwnedBy` + `TransactionDao.activeOwnedBy`; Settings → Profile → Account "Reset finances" entry + confirm dialog (counts = transactions + accounts; live-disabled confirm when offline). ADR-0037 + `CONTEXT.md` amended to the new design.

**Tests:** reworked `ResetFinancesRepositoryImplTest` (own transactions soft-deleted + own accounts zeroed incl. archived; partner/shared/already-deleted untouched; account survives as a row; single-transaction) + `ResetFinancesUseCaseTest` (password re-auth success/failure gate). JVM-only.

**Verify:** on-device — trigger reset on a test account (e.g. testdev14) holding transactions/budgets/recurring rules/savings goals + contributions; confirm transactions gone + every account balance reads ₱0, while budgets/recurring/savings-progress/categories/notes survive; confirm the confirm button is disabled with the "need internet" hint when offline.

## Item 20 — Sign-out "Unsynced changes" wedge ✅ DONE `a689597` (2026-07-11)

- **Status:** DONE **2026-07-11** (`a689597`; partner-debts/payments follow-up `aad6e4d`) — root-caused live on testdev15's device (on-device DB inspection), device unblocked the same day, then **grilled + fixed on Opus** (creator-only un-share + flip-model push ownership filter). All three parts shipped; 804 unit tests green. The deferred partner-debts/payments F1 residual is now also closed (`aad6e4d`, 812 tests) — see the follow-up section at the end of this item. **Model: Opus.** Non-paywall. Fix summary at the end of this item; the sections below are the original diagnosis, kept for the record.

**Symptom:** signing out shows the "Unsynced changes" confirm dialog ([MainActivity.kt:361](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/MainActivity.kt#L361), ADR-0021) persistently, even while online. The guard works as designed — `AuthViewModel.signOut` runs `syncEngine.pushOnly()` first and, if it *throws*, warns before wiping local data so unpushed changes aren't silently lost. The real question was *why* the push kept throwing.

**ROOT CAUSE — `unshareAccount` produces an un-pushable "poison" row when the un-sharer ≠ the account's creator.** [`AccountRepositoryImpl.unshareAccount`](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/accounts/data/AccountRepositoryImpl.kt#L105-L119) reverts a shared account to `createdBy` "regardless of who un-shares" (per the ADR-0018 comment), stamping the local row `userId = createdBy, coupleId = null, pendingSync = true`. When **partner B unshares an account partner A created**, the local row now claims `user_id = A` with no `couple_id` — which the `accounts` RLS (`accounts_owner: user_id = auth.uid()` **OR** `accounts_couple: couple_id = auth_couple_id()`) forbids B's session to write. B can satisfy neither clause, so the push is rejected.

**Why one poison row wedges the *whole* table (blast radius):** [`SupabaseAccountRemoteSource.push`](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/accounts/data/remote/SupabaseAccountRemoteSource.kt#L14) sends the table's entire dirty set as a **single atomic `client.from("accounts").upsert(rows)`**. Postgres fails the whole statement on the one poison row, so **none** of the dirty rows clear `pendingSync`, and `pushOnly()` throws every time. `SyncEngine`'s "per-table isolation" (F1) isolates tables from each other but **not rows within a table** — so the accounts table stays wedged forever, wedging sign-out.

**Why it "self-resolved" in the 2026-07-10 sighting:** the poison row finally converged via a **pull**, not a push — partner A later edited the same account, A's newer `updated_at` won LWW, and `applyPullBatch` overwrote B's local poison row with `pending_sync = false`, dropping it from the dirty batch. (The 2026-07-10 "zero POST/PATCH, threw client-side before HTTP" note was a mis-read of the API logs / a different window — the current, verified cause is an RLS-rejected `upsert`, which *is* an HTTP 4xx.)

**Concrete repro data (testdev15 = Wifey `e7aaba95`, paired with testdev17 = Hubby `8bdbcef8`, couple `31b0580e`):** 6 dirty `accounts` rows; 5 were legitimately Wifey/couple-owned and pushable. The 1 poison row was **"Bank"** (`a3144b6d`) — a couple account **created by Hubby** that Wifey had unshared, leaving it local-stamped `userId = 8bdbcef8, coupleId = null`. Server still held it as couple-owned. That one row failed the batch and froze all 6.

**Remediation applied 2026-07-11 (device only, no code change):** reset the local "Bank" row to the server-canonical shared state (`userId = null, coupleId = 31b0580e, serverRev = 1095, pendingSync = 0`) directly in the on-device Room DB (app force-stopped, WAL consolidated, integrity-checked, written back). Next foreground sync then pushed the 5 legit rows (Cash/Maribank → Wifey-personal; CIMB Joint/UB Plat CC/Gotyme inserted) and Bank stayed couple-owned — **verified 0 dirty on device + rows landed on staging.** ⚠️ Re-unsharing a partner-created account reintroduces the wedge until the code fix ships.

**How it was caught (reusable recipe, no instrumentation needed):** `adb exec-out run-as com.iponlove.app.staging cat databases/ipon.db` (+ `-wal`/`-shm`) → local `sqlite3` → `SELECT … WHERE pendingSync = 1` per synced table to find the stuck rows, then compare each dirty row's local `userId`/`coupleId` against the server (Supabase MCP `execute_sql`) and the table's RLS `with_check`. The mismatched-ownership row is the culprit. (Room columns are camelCase: `pendingSync`, `serverRev`, `updatedAt`.)

**Fix direction (to grill, then build on Opus):**
1. **`unshareAccount` must not queue an own-push for a row the local session can't own.** When un-sharer ≠ creator, either (a) route the revert-to-creator through a server RPC (like `unpair`'s revert) so the server, not B's client, performs the ownership change, and locally demote the row to a partner replica / purge it per ADR-0004/0005; or (b) forbid unsharing a partner-created account (creator-only unshare) — a couples-governance decision. Same hazard may exist in the parallel `unshareGoal` path — check `SavingsGoalRepositoryImpl`.
2. **Row-level push isolation** so one rejected row can't wedge a whole table's batch — e.g. fall back to per-row upsert on batch failure and quarantine the offender, or pre-filter un-ownable rows out of `dirtyRows()`. Extends F1 from per-table to per-row.
3. **Sign-out UX (the open question):** should one permanently-unpushable row wedge sign-out indefinitely? The current confirm's only escape ("sign out anyway") discards *all* pending edits, not just the poison one.

**Fix shipped 2026-07-11 `a689597` (grilled → built on Opus).** Three parts, all client-side (no schema migration, no RPC):

1. **Creator-only un-share (root cause).** `unshareAccount`/`unshareCategory` no-op when `createdBy != me` (mirrors goals' owner-only `mutateOwn`); the "Make personal" menu item is hidden for non-creators via a new `Account.isCreator`/`Category.isCreator` (mapper computes `createdBy == currentUserId`). A non-creator can no longer create the poison row. **ADR-0018 amended** accordingly (unpair's server-side revert is unchanged).
2. **Flip-model push ownership filter (blast-radius + F1 residual).** `AccountTableSyncer`/`CategoryTableSyncer`/`BudgetTableSyncer` override `dirtyRows()` to push only rows this session can own — `isLocallyPushable(userId, coupleId, me, myCoupleId)` in `core/sync` (own personal, or a couple row of the *current* couple). Un-ownable rows (partner-owned, stale-couple from an unpair race, or a legacy poison row) are skipped as benign local orphans, so one can never wedge the atomic batch again. Budgets are included for the unpair-race even though they have no un-share bug. Generalises the `goal_contributions` F1 guard (ADR-0025).
3. **Sign-out guard (ADR-0021) left unchanged** — with (1)+(2), `pushOnly()` no longer throws on a permanently-unpushable row, so the confirm now only fires for genuine offline unsynced edits, which is correct.

**Not affected (audited 2026-07-11):** only accounts + categories had the un-share bug. Savings goals & notes keep `user_id = creator` (owner-retained). Budgets/partner-debts are couple-scoped and pushable by either partner — no revert-to-creator path. Transactions/recurring are always owner-held. See the audit table in the conversation / the "flip XOR check" tables (`accounts`, `categories`, `budgets`).

**Tests:** `PushOwnershipTest` (predicate), mapper `isCreator` cases, repo non-creator no-op (accounts + categories), and the three syncer filter tests — all green in the 804-test suite.

**Partner-debts/payments follow-up — DONE `aad6e4d` (2026-07-11, Opus).** The deferred F1 residual for the two always-couple tables is now closed with the same push-ownership approach — straight pattern-following of `a689597`, no grill needed (the only new call, own-predicate-vs-reuse, resolved by reading: these are **not** flip-model, so they get their own predicate). Client-side only, no schema/Room/RPC change (stays **v25**).
- **Not flip-model:** `partner_debts.couple_id` is `NOT NULL`, no `user_id` flip; RLS is purely `couple_id = auth_couple_id()`. So a new sibling predicate `isCoupleRowPushable(coupleId, myCoupleId)` in `core/sync/PushOwnership.kt` (couple-scoped counterpart of `isLocallyPushable`), rather than muddying the flip-model one by passing a null `userId`.
- **Payments have no `couple_id`:** reached via `debt_id -> partner_debts.couple_id`, matching the payment RLS subquery. `DebtPaymentTableSyncer.dirtyRows()` resolves `myCoupleId`, builds the current couple's local debt-id set (`debtIdsForCouple`, **no `is_deleted` filter** — the RLS subquery has none, so a payment against a soft-deleted-but-same-couple debt still pushes), and keeps only payments whose `debtId` is in it. Unpaired (`myCoupleId == null`) → empty set → all skipped.
- **`PartnerDebtTableSyncer.dirtyRows()`** filters debts by `coupleId == myCoupleId` (via `coupleIdOf` off the local users row, same source as `AccountDao`).
- **Netting undisturbed (the pre-build caveat, confirmed):** the filter is push-*selection* only — never mutates a row, id, `counterDebtId`, or `isNetting` — and keys off `debtId` (matching RLS, which ignores `counter_debt_id`), so deterministic-UUIDv5 convergence is untouched. A dedicated test asserts a netting row pushes off its parent even when its counter-debt resolves to no local row.
- **Files:** `core/sync/PushOwnership.kt` (+`isCoupleRowPushable`), `PartnerDebtDao` (+`coupleIdOf`/`debtIdsForCouple`), `PartnerDebtTableSyncer` + `DebtPaymentTableSyncer` (`dirtyRows()` overrides, `CurrentUserProvider` injected — no DI-module change, constructor injection).
- **Tests (+8, suite 804→812):** 3 `PushOwnershipTest` cases (`isCoupleRowPushable`: current/stale/unpaired) + 5 `PartnerDebtTableSyncerTest` filter cases (debt stale-skip, debt unpaired-skip, payment parent-in-couple-only, payment netting-keys-off-parent, payment unpaired-skip); `FakePartnerDebtDao` extended with the two new queries. `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green. Same narrow-race caveat as the parent fix — not separately on-device reproducible; unit coverage is the verification.

## Item 23 — Archived entity label fallback in Records & Budgets (⏸️ DEFERRED — needs tester feedback)

- **Status:** ⏸️ **DEFERRED 2026-07-11** — booked but intentionally **not scheduled**; Alvin wants **tester feedback first** before deciding whether it's a bug to fix or the intended signal. Split out of [Item 19](#item-19--manage-surface-archived-accountscategories-so-they-can-be-unarchived-) to keep that slice tightly scoped. **Model (if built): Sonnet, low effort.** Non-paywall.
- **Independent** — pure display-time label resolution, no schema/sync/data change.

**Surfaced 2026-07-11** while confirming Item 19's archive semantics. Records and Budgets resolve a category/account **name from its id** via a lookup map built from `observeCategories()` / `observeAccounts()` at the default `includeArchived = false`. So a **historical row pointing at a now-archived entity** drops out of the map and falls back to a generic label:
- **Records list** ([TransactionsViewModel.toListItem](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsViewModel.kt#L161)) — a transaction whose **category** was archived reads **"Uncategorized"** (`categoryNames[categoryId] ?: "Uncategorized"`); whose **account** was archived reads **"Account"** (`accountNames[accountId] ?: "Account"`).
- **Budgets** ([BudgetsViewModel](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/budgets/presentation/BudgetsViewModel.kt#L78)) — an existing budget on a now-archived category reads **"Category"** (`categoryNames[it] ?: "Category"`); the budget still tracks spending correctly, only the name degrades.

**The inconsistency:** [Analysis](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/analysis/presentation/AnalysisViewModel.kt#L83) deliberately observes `includeArchived = true` so archived categories **keep their label** in the donut/flow; Recurring materialization does the same. Records and Budgets never got that treatment, so the **same archived category is labeled three different ways** depending on the screen. It is **purely cosmetic** — no data loss (the row still carries its `categoryId`/`accountId`), and **unarchiving restores every label instantly** (the entity re-enters the map).

**The product question to answer with tester feedback (why it's deferred, not just built):** is an archived category *supposed* to keep naming its old transactions in Records (consistent with Analysis), or is **"Uncategorized"** the intended cue that "this category is retired"? Don't change the behavior until this is decided.

**If built (the shape):** Records is a one-line switch to `observeCategories(includeArchived = true)` / `observeAccounts(includeArchived = true)` (it uses the list only for label lookup, not a picker). Budgets is a **two-line split** — build the label map from an archived-inclusive observe, but keep the **new-budget picker** (`expenseCategories = categories.filter { it.type == EXPENSE }`) filtered to **active** categories so archived ones don't reappear as budgetable options. (The Add-Transaction / Quick-add / Recurring-editor pickers stay `false` — archived items must not be offered for *new* activity.)

**Verify (if built):** archive a category with existing transactions + a budget → Records rows keep the real name (not "Uncategorized"), the budget row keeps its name (not "Category"), Analysis unchanged; the archived category does **not** appear in the Add-Transaction picker or the new-budget picker; unarchive → everything unchanged.

## Item 24 — Privacy mask doesn't cover the Analysis calendar chart 🔴

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `52fb40d`** (2026-07-13, on-device verified by Alvin). **Model: Sonnet, low effort** (built on Opus — pure UI wiring, Sonnet-class). Non-paywall (privacy). Found 2026-07-13 while building Item 18. No schema/Room change (stays **v25**).
- **As built:** exactly the plan below. Mirrors Item 18's glyph threading — captured `val privacyOn = LocalPrivacyMode.current` in composable scope (beside the Item 18 `glyph` capture) and threaded it into the non-composable draw code through all four `compactAmount` call sites (income+expense paired, plus the two single-row cases). `compactAmount` gained a `masked: Boolean` param + branch that returns `"$sign•••"`.
- **Masked-cell rendering (the open decision, resolved):** short `•••` token, **keeping the sign + row colour** (green income / red expense) but never the peso value or glyph — **not** a blank cell. Rationale: matches the app-wide "mask the value, keep the context" behaviour (`money()` renders `•••••`, not nothing); a blank cell would additionally hide *that a day had activity*, more aggressive than the rest of the masked UI. `•••` (3 dots) instead of the app's `•••••` so it fits the narrow 64dp cell.
- **Files touched:** `feature/analysis/presentation/components/DailyNetCalendarChart.kt` (only). +16/−6.
- **Tests:** none added — pure Canvas draw wiring; `compactAmount` is a `private` UI helper whose existing k/M formatting was never unit-tested either, so the mask branch follows the same verify-by-running precedent (Testing Policy). `testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green. On-device verified by Alvin (Hide amounts ON → Calendar cells masked; OFF → real amounts return).

**Bug:** the Analysis → **Calendar** sub-tab's per-day amounts bypass the Item 15 privacy mask. [`DailyNetCalendarChart.compactAmount`](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/analysis/presentation/components/DailyNetCalendarChart.kt) formats each cell with its own compact formatter (drawn on a Canvas), never routing through `money()` / `LocalPrivacyMode`. So with **"Hide amounts" ON, the calendar still shows real daily income/expense** (e.g. "+₱5.0k" / "+$5.0k") — a leak the global mask was meant to close. (Item 18 threaded the display *symbol* into this same formatter but deliberately left the mask out, as a separate concern.)

**Change:** thread `LocalPrivacyMode.current` into the chart the same way Item 18 captured the symbol glyph (a `val` in composable scope closed over by the draw code), and render the cell **masked** when on. Decide the masked-cell rendering — a short mask token (e.g. `•••`) vs. a blank cell (the dot-grid may read cleaner than "•••••" in a 64dp cell).

**Verify:** Hide amounts ON → Analysis → Calendar cells are masked (Donut/Flow already mask via `money()`); OFF → real amounts return.

## Item 25 — Privacy mode defaults ON when the app opens (auto-hide per session) 🟡

- **Status:** PLANNED — **needs one decision before build.** **Model: Sonnet, low–medium.** Non-paywall (privacy). Requested by Alvin 2026-07-13.

**Request:** on opening the app, amounts should be **hidden by default** (private); the user reveals them per session rather than the current "defaults visible, persists your last choice."

**Decision to settle (the shape hinges on this):**
- **(a) One-time default flip** — Privacy mode simply *defaults* ON (fresh install / first run), then persists the user's toggles like today. Simplest: flip the DataStore default in `PrivacyModeRepositoryImpl` from `false` to `true`. But once a user turns it off it stays off — it does **not** re-hide "when opening the app" again.
- **(b) Recurring auto-hide (the literal reading of "default when opening the app")** — every cold open (and likely every foreground resume past the app-lock 30s grace) resets to ON; "revealed" is a **per-session, non-persisted** state. Interacts with `AppLockManager`'s grace window — decide whether a quick background bounce keeps amounts revealed or re-hides.

Leaning **(b)** given the wording; confirm before building. Ties into the reveal entry points already built in Item 15 (Settings switch + the Accounts/Analysis eye icons).

**Verify:** reopen the app (cold, and after a >grace background) → amounts hidden until revealed; the eye icons/Settings switch still reveal.

## Item 28 — Media-cap gate fires before the photo picker opens (S8 wart, pre-flip rider) 🟢

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `4966e01`** (2026-07-14, on-device verified by Alvin). Decided on the 2026-07-13 paywall flip re-grill (paywall doc §10.7b row A7): **fix pre-flip**, reversing S8's "accept unless it bites" deferral. **Model: Sonnet, low effort** (built on Opus this session). Paywall follow-up; **must land before S13** (the enforcement-ON rehearsal). Dormant-safe: with enforcement OFF the pre-check short-circuits to `Allowed`, so nothing changes until flip day. No Room/schema change (stays **v25**).

**Wart (from S8, `feb2d23`):** the media-cap gates check *after* the system photo picker returns — only the chosen URI reaches `AddTransactionViewModel.onImagePicked` / `NoteEditorViewModel.addImage`. So an enforced free user at their cap taps "Add photo", browses the gallery, picks a photo, **and only then** sees the cap sheet. Functionally correct (nothing added, T1 freeze holds) but "made me pick, then refused" — a first-impression insult on flip day, and the fix is cheap because the count is already in-editor UI state (no DAO, no async).

**Change:** run the same `Check…CapUseCase` at the **"Add photo" tap**, before launching the picker — at the cap → show the existing `CapReachedSheet` immediately and never open the picker; under the cap → launch the picker as today (keep the post-picker check as the backstop). Three launch sites: AddTransaction add + edit routes, NoteEditor.

**Verify:** enforcement ON (staging flip), free account at each cap → tap "Add photo" → cap sheet appears with **no picker**; under cap → picker opens and the photo lands. Dormant → byte-identical to today. Extend the two S8 test files with the tap-time decision case if any new VM seam is introduced (the check itself is already covered).

**As-built (`4966e01`, 2026-07-14):** two new VM seams take a `launchPicker: () -> Unit` — `AddTransactionViewModel.onAddPhotoTap` and `NoteEditorViewModel.onAddImageTap` — that run the existing `checkReceiptPhotoCap` / `checkNoteAttachmentCap` at tap time: `Allowed` → invoke `launchPicker()` (unchanged flow); `Blocked` → `raiseUpsell(...)` and the picker never opens. `AddTransactionScreen`'s `onAddReceipt` and `NoteEditorScreen`'s add-image `IconButton` now wrap their launcher call in the seam; the post-picker `onImagePicked` / `addImage` checks stay as backstops. Two code files per screen cover all three routes (AddTransaction's add + edit share `AddTransactionContent`). **No new JVM test:** neither editor VM has a test harness (deferred per the Testing Policy), and the tap invokes the *identical* use-case check at the *identical* counts the two S8 cap-use-case test files already prove — a duplicate test would be theater; the ordering is verified on-device. On-device verified by Alvin via a temporary staging `enforcement_enabled` flip (cap sheet at the cap with no picker; picker opens under the cap), then flipped back to dormant.

## Item 29 — Coach-mark tour bleeds across screens + ring has no padding 🟢

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `8ba95b0`** (2026-07-14, on-device verified by Alvin). **Model: Sonnet, low effort.** Found 2026-07-14 by Alvin while testing the tutorial. No schema/Room change (stays **v25**).

**Bug 1 (tour bleed):** a tour armed on one screen (e.g. `RECORDS`, on first visit to Transactions) never ended when the user navigated away — `TutorialUiState.active` stayed true. The tagged target's bounds also never left `CoachMarkState.bounds` once its screen was gone, so the ring kept drawing at the *old* screen's stale coordinates over whatever screen came next (e.g. Analysis), and — since another tour was still "active" — the destination screen's own first-visit tour was blocked from starting ([TutorialViewModel.maybeStartTour](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/tutorial/presentation/TutorialViewModel.kt) no-ops while `_uiState.value.active`). This is also what made Bug 2 look like a positioning bug: the ring visible over `AddTransactionScreen`'s Type row was actually a leftover tour's stale ring, not the `TRANSACTION_ENTRY` tour's own (correctly-anchored) one.

**Bug 2 (ring has zero padding):** independent of the bleed — [CoachMarkOverlay](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/CoachMark.kt) drew the highlight ring at the target's *exact* raw layout bounds with no inset, so it hugged tight enough to visually clip the "Type" label / button-row edges once the correct target was on screen.

**Fix:**
- `CoachMark.kt` — the `@Composable Modifier.coachMarkTarget(key)` overload (used by screen targets, not the persistent bottom-bar chrome) now unregisters its bounds via `DisposableEffect(onDispose)` when the tagged composable leaves composition. The ring is drawn inflated by a 6dp outward inset instead of the raw target rect, and the tooltip's gap is measured from that inset ring so the card doesn't crowd it.
- `TutorialViewModel.kt` — new `dismissForNavigation()`: clears the active tour without marking it seen (so it re-arms on the next real visit), freeing the single-active-tour slot.
- `IponApp.kt` — a `LaunchedEffect` keyed on the active step watches `coachState.boundsOf(key)` via `snapshotFlow`: once the target has laid out, it waits for the bounds to disappear (navigation away) and calls `dismissForNavigation()`.

**Files touched:** `core/ui/CoachMark.kt`, `feature/tutorial/presentation/TutorialViewModel.kt`, `navigation/IponApp.kt`.
**Tests:** none added — pure Compose overlay/navigation-lifecycle wiring, no new tier-1 logic; `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green (no regressions). On-device verified by Alvin: Records → Analysis no longer shows a stale tooltip; ⊕ New Transaction's Type row ring is correctly sized/positioned with breathing room.
